title: Phishing message quarantined before delivery
sourceData: Microsoft Sentinel Training Lab — MailGuard365_Threats_CL / SEG_MailGuard_CL
summary: A phishing message from a domain used in a live campaign against this tenant was correctly quarantined. The same sender infrastructure reached other mailboxes, which is where the actual exposure lies.

discriminatingEvidence.question: Was this message delivered?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: union MailGuard365_Threats_CL, SEG_MailGuard_CL | where RecipientAddress has 'admin@' | project TimeGenerated, SenderAddress, ThreatVerdict, Action
discriminatingEvidence.expected: Action = Quarantine — it never reached the mailbox

discriminatingEvidence.question: Did the same sender infrastructure reach anyone else?
discriminatingEvidence.kql: union MailGuard365_Threats_CL, SEG_MailGuard_CL | where SenderDomain has 'malicious-infra' or SenderIP == '198.51.100.42' | project RecipientAddress, ThreatVerdict, Action
discriminatingEvidence.expected: Messages to mirage@ from the same infrastructure were Allowed

trap: Two opposite errors are available. Closing it as a false positive ignores that the message was genuinely malicious. Escalating it as a compromise ignores that the control held. The useful finding is neither: the same campaign got through to a different mailbox, and that is what warrants follow-up.
evaluatorNotes: Rewards lateral thinking — the right answer for this alert is 'no impact', but a good investigation notices the related delivered messages and says so. Pairs directly with mirage-account-takeover, which is where that campaign led.
